Pursuant to 10 CFR 50.54(a)(4), Florida Power & Light Company (FPL), acting on behalf of itself and
as agent for NextEra Energy Point Beach, LLC, NextEra Energy Seabrook, LLC, and NextEra Energy
Duane Arnold, LLC [hereinafter collectively referred to as "NextEra"], hereby requests changes to
Quality Assurance Topical Reports (QATR) FPL-1 for Turkey Point Nuclear Plant, Units 3 and 4
(Turkey Point), St. Lucie Nuclear Plant, Units 1 and 2 (St. Lucie), Point Beach Nuclear Plant, Units 1
and 2 (Point Beach), and Seabrook Station Unit 1 (Seabrook), and to QATR FPL-3 for the Duane
Arnold Energy Center (Duane Arnold), regarding licensed operator eligibility which constitutes a
reduction in Quality Assurance commitment. Specifically, NextEra requests NRC approval of a
licensed operator eligibility alternative pursuant to the allowance in 10 CFR 55.31 (a)(4) to either detail
an applicant's qualifications or certify successful completion of a systems approach to training (SAT)
based, Commission-approved training program . NextEra continues to commit to the operator license
candidate eligibility guidelines of National Academy for Nuclear Training ACAD 10-001, "Guidelines
for Initial Training and Qualification of Licensed Operators," as endorsed by NUREG-1021 , "Operator
Licensing Examination Standards for Power Reactors," Revision 12 (ADAMS Accession No.
ML21256A276), for meeting the SAT-based certification option of 10 CFR 55.31(a)(4). The proposed
alternative, titled the "NextGen Ops Program Plan," is NextEra's nuclear-focused development
pathway for college students and other NextEra employees progressing toward licensed operator

initial training, providing an equivalent or superior basis for ensuring candidate qualification consistent
with 10 CFR Part 66 and the objectives of NUREG-1021.

This request seeks NRC approval of a method that NextEra has developed to provide an equivalent
degree of assurance of licensed operator qualification as those which the NRC has previously
endorsed. Consistent with the NUREG-1021 ES-2.2 guidance slating that the NRC cannot alter or
waive education and experience requirements that are part of the National Nuclear Accrediting Board
(NNAB)-accredited facility licensee training program, NextEra requests approval of the alternative
approach within the context of an accredited training program for meeting 55.31(a}(4). For any use of
the altemative approach within the context of the accredited training program, NextEra would be solely
responsible for demonstrating to the NNAB that the use of this alternative was acceptable.

The enclosures to this letter provide the description, evaluation, and requisite licensing actions for the
proposed alternative. Enclosure 1 provides an evaluation of the proposed revision to the Quality
Assurance Topical Reports (QATRs) FPL-1 (Turkey Point, St. Lucie, Point Beach, Seabrook) and FPL-
3 (Duane Amold). Enclosure 2 provides the NextGen Ops Program Plan which details the framework
and implementation plan for the proposed alternative. Enclosures 3 and 4, respectively, contain Senior
Reactor Operator Eligibility Pathway Comparisons and Reactor Operator Eligibility Pathway
Comparisons which demonstrate how the proposed altematlve meets the intent of the ACAD guidance
to provide an equivalent assurance of licensed operator qualification. Enclosure 5 provides the
proposed QATR FPL-1 markup and Enclosure 6 provides the proposed QATR FPL-3 markup.

NextEra requests approval of the enclosed QATR change request within one year of satisfactory
acceptance. The proposed change shall be implemented within six months of either NRC approval or
expiration of the 60-days referenced In 10 CFR) 50.54(a)(4)(iv) for acceptance review completion.

Changes to the quality assurance program description included or referenced in the Safety Analysis
Report shall be regarded as accepted by the Commission upon receipt of a letter to this effect from
the appropriate reviewing office of the Commission or 60 days after submittal to the Commission,
whichever occurs first.

This letter contains new regulatory commitments.

Should you have any questions regarding this submission, please contact Ms. Maribel Valdez, Senior.
Manager, Operating Fleet Licensing Manager, at 561-904-5164.

        NEXTERA QUALITY ASSURANCE TOPICAL REPORT (QATR) CHANGE REQUEST FOR
         LICENSED OPERA TOR CANDIDATE QUALIFICATION ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS

1.0     SUMMARY DESCRIPTION

Florida Power & Light Company (FPL), acting on behalf of itself and as agent for NextEra Energy Point
Beach, LLC, NextEra Energy Seabrook, LLC, and NextEra Energy Duane Arnold, LLC [hereinafter
collectively referred to as "NextEra"], requests changes to Quality Assurance Topical Reports (QATR)
FPL-1 for Turkey Point Nuclear Plant, Units 3 and 4, St. Lucie Nuclear Plant, Units 1 and 2, Point
Beach Nuclear Plant, Units 1 and 2, and Seabrook Station Unit 1, and to QATR FPL-3 for the Duane
Arnold Energy Center, regarding licensed operator eligibility which constitutes a reduction in Quality
Assurance commitment. Specifically, NextEra requests NRC approval of a licensed operator eligibility
alternative pursuant to the allowance in 10 CFR 55.31 (a)(4) to either detail an applicant's qualifications
or certify successful completion of a SAT-based, Commission-approved training program training
program. NextEra continues to commit to the operator license candidate eligibility guidelines of
National Academy for Nuclear Training ACAD 10-001 (Reference 4.1) as endorsed by NUREG-1021,
"Operator Licensing Examination Standards for Power Reactors," Revision 12 (Reference 4.2), for
meeting the SAT-based certification option. The proposed alternative, titled the "NextGen Ops
Program Plan," is NextEra's nuclear-focused development pathway for college students and other
NextEra employees progressing toward licensed operator initial training, providing an equivalent or
superior basis

This request seeks NRC approval of a method that NextEra has developed to provide an equivalent
degree of assurance of licensed operator qualification as those which the NRC has previously
endorsed. Consistent with the NUREG-1021 ES-2.2 guidance stating that the NRC cannot alter or
waive education and experience requirements that are part of the National Nuclear Accrediting Board
(NNAB)-accredited facility licensee training program, NextEra requests approval of the alternative
approach within the context of an accredited training program for meeting 55.31 (a)(4). For any use of
the alternative approach within the context of the accredited training program, NextEra would be solely
responsible for demonstrating to the NNAB that the use of this alternative was acceptable.

Included within this Enclosure is an evaluation of the proposed change. This Enclosure also provides
a description of the revised commitments in QATRs FPL-1 and FPL-3. No changes to the facility
Technical Specifications (TS) or the associated TS Bases are proposed.


2.0     DETAILED DESCRIPTION

2.1.    Background

10 CFR 55.31 describes the information that is required to be provided to the NRC to apply for the
licensing of an operator or senior operator. Specifically, 55.31 (a)(4) states, in part, that the applicant
shall do the following [emphasis added]:

       Provide evidence that the applicant has successfully completed the facility licensee's
       requirements to be licensed as an operator or senior operator and of the facility licensee's need
       for an operator or a senior operator to perform assigned duties. An authorized representative of
       the facility licensee shall certify this evidence on Form NRC-398. This certification must include
       details of the applicant's qualifications, and details on courses of instruction administered by the
       facility licensee, and describe the nature of the training received at the facility, and the startup
       and shutdown experience received. In lieu of these details, the Commission may accept
       certification that the applicant has successfully completed a Commission-approved training

        program that is based on a systems approach to training [SATl and that uses a simulation facility
        acceptable to the Commission under§ 55.45(b) of this part. ..

Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.8, Revision 4 (Reference 4.3), describes methods that the NRC considers
acceptable for use in implementing the requirements of 10 CFR 50.34(b)(6)(i), 1O CFR 50.120, and
10 CFR 52.79(a)(26). The NRC states that compliance with this regulatory guidance is not required,
and that different methods and solutions will be deemed acceptable if they provide a sufficient basis
and information for the NRC staff to verify that the proposed alternative demonstrates compliance with
the appropriate NRC regulations. Under Revision 4 of RG 1.8, the NRC noted that the National
Academy for Nuclear Training (NANT) and NUREG-1021 qualification standards met or exceeded
those of ANSI/ANS-3.1-2014 (Reference 4.4) for operator licensing and, furthermore, that the NANT
qualification standards better aligned with the SAT-based facility license training programs. Upon this
basis, the NRC removed the applicability of 10 CFR Part 55 from RG 1.8, Revision 4, and elected to
instead address NRC guidance for operator license qualifications solely in NUREG-1021. NUREG-
1021, Revision 12, ES-2.2 states that to be accredited by the National Nuclear Accrediting Board
(NNAB), a facility licensee training program must implement the NANT education and experience
guidelines (e.g., ACAD 10-001 ). However, the NRC also notes within ES-2.2 that substitutions or
determinations allowed by NANT guidelines for qualification and training do not require NRC
approval.

ACAD 10-001, "Guidelines for Initial Training and Qualification of Licensed Operators," (Revision 2)
section 1, states, in part, that "Members of [National Academy for Nuclear Training] NANT may use
different approaches or methods than those defined herein, but members are expected to meet the
intent of these guidelines." 1

NextEra has analyzed the alternative eligibility guidelines described by the NextGen Ops Program and
determined that these guidelines satisfy the intent of ACAD 10-001 and are therefore acceptable for
use within the context of NextEra's associated accredited training programs. These analyses are
documented in Enclosure 3, "Senior Reactor Operator Eligibility Pathway Comparisons," and
"Enclosure 4 Reactor Operator Eligibility Pathway Comparisons." NextEra is engaging with INPO in
parallel with making this regulatory submittal to ensure alignment with this interpretation. NextEra
remains solely responsible for demonstrating to the National Nuclear Accrediting Board that the use
of this alternative is acceptable within the context of its accredited training programs.

At present, QATR FPL-1 commits to Regulatory Guide 1.8, Revision 4, while QATR FPL-3 commits
to a systematic approach to training (SAT). NextEra proposes to revise QATR FPL-1 and QATR FPL-
3 to reduce the existing commitment from strict adherence to ACAD 10-001 eligibility criteria, as
endorsed under NUREG-1021, Revision 12, by authorizing supplemental alternative eligibility
pathways under the NextGen Ops Program Plan. The proposed change would constitute a voluntary
reduction in the scope of the existing licensing commitment, replacing a single eligibility standard with
a framework that permits additional qualifying pathways for Reactor Operator (RO) and Senior Reactor
Operator (SRO) license candidates.

2.2.    NRC Policy Background

50 FR 11147 (1985), "Commission Policy Statement on Training and Qualification of Nuclear Plant
Personnel," states, in part, the following [emphasis added]:

        Notwithstanding this Policy guidance, regulations in 10 CFR Part 55 regarding licensed
        operators will continue to be the basis for evaluation of applications for operators' licenses ...

        The NRC and industry recognize that the qualifications of personnel at nuclear power plants
        should be commensurate with the requirements of the jobs they perform. Since the INPO-
        managed accreditation and evaluation programs are performance-based, this policy statement
        assumes that training programs for those positions covered will provide appropriately qualified
        personnel. For positions outside the scope of the INPO-managed accreditation program, for
        licensed operators and senior operators, and for all personnel at facilities applying for an
        operating license, NRC staff will continue to review qualifications in accordance with appropriate
        regulatory policy guidance ...

54 FR 33639 (1989), "Commission Policy Statement Education for Senior Reactor Operators and Shift
Supervisors at Nuclear Power Plants," states, in part, the following [emphasis added]:

        The Commission believes that the level of engineering and technical knowledge of shift
        operating personnel has a direct bearing on the safety of nuclear power plants. Accordingly, the
        Commission believes that the safety of commercial power reactors is enhanced by having on
        each shift a team of NRG-licensed professionals that combine technical and academic
        knowledge with plant-specific training and substantial hands-on operating experience ...

In summary, NextEra proposes to implement a "NextGen Ops Program Plan," that serves a dual purpose
of ensuring program success while providing an increased candidate pool of quantity, quality and
diversity. NextGen Ops is NextEra Energy's nuclear-focused development pathway designed to introduce
college students and other NextEra employees to nuclear plant operations in a way that meets both the
intent of ACAD 10-001, the requirements of NUREG-1021, and the relevant NRC Policy Statements.

2.3.    QATR Description of Changes

The QATR is the top-level policy document that establishes the manner in which quality is to be
achieved and presents NextEra's overall philosophy regarding achievement and assurance of quality.
Implementing documents assign more detailed responsibilities and requirements and define the
organizational interfaces involved in conducting activities within the scope of the QATR. Compliance
with the QATR and implementing documents is mandatory for personnel directly or indirectly
associated with implementation of the Quality Assurance Program (QAP).

NextEra proposes an update to its existing licensed operator training eligibility fleet commitments
contained in QATR FPL-1 and QATR FPL-3. Specifically, the following addition to Section A.5,
"Personnel Training and Qualification", of QATR FPL-1 and QATR FPL-3 is proposed:

       Notwithstanding the specific education and experience criteria under NUREG-1021,
       NextEra will utilize the NextGen Ops Program Plan to supplement candidate qualification
       eligibility and entry into the Licensed Operating Training Program.

       1. NextEra commits to meeting the licensed operator eligibility guidelines for Senior
          Reactor Operator and Reactor Operator candidates presented under ACAD 10-001 and
          endorsed under NUREG-1021, as supplemented by the additional "Senior Reactor

       2. NextEra will maintain the general contents, durations, and structures of the NextGen

          (e.g., NEI 06-13A).

Enclosures 5 and 6 to this letter provide the affected pages of QATR FPL-1 and QATR FPL-3, marked
up to show the proposed changes, respectively.

2.4.    Reason for the Proposed Change

The proposed changes constitute a voluntary reduction in commitments contained in QATR FPL-1
and QATR FPL-3. The existing commitments require adherence to the specific education and
experience criteria of ACAD 10-001, as endorsed under NUREG-1021, Revision 12. NextEra
proposes to reduce these commitments by authorizing supplemental alternative eligibility pathways
that meet the intent of ACAD 10-001. This reduction in commitments is permissible because: ( 1)
compliance with Regulatory Guides is not mandatory per NRC policy; (2) RG 1.8, Revision 4,
acknowledges that alternative methods are acceptable if they provide a sufficient basis for NRC
licensing findings; and (3) the proposed NextGen Ops Program Plan provides an equivalent or superior
basis for ensuring licensed operator candidate qualification consistent with 10 CFR Part 55 and
NUREG-1021 objectives.

The proposed alternative, titled "NextGen Ops" would be NextEra's nuclear-focused development
pathway for college students and other NextEra employees seeking to enter the licensed operator
initial training program, whereby participants would work alongside licensed reactor operators and
plant staff, learning fundamentals of NRG-regulated operations and safety culture as they progress
toward eventual operator licensure. Though the proposed alternative would constitute a reduction in
a Quality Assurance Program commitment, the NextGen Ops Program Plan would provide an
equivalent or superior basis for ensuring licensed operator candidate qualification consistent with 10
CFR Part 55 and NUREG-1021 objectives.

3.0    CONCLUSION OF CONTINUED QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM COMPLIANCE

An operator license candidate that completes a SAT-based training program has been trained
according to objectives and materials that were, themselves, derived from an analysis of the job to be
performed. At the conclusion of that training program, the operator is tested on a systematic sampling
of knowledge and abilities that are associated with job tasks of relatively high importance. In
completing this training and examination process, an operator has demonstrated, irrespective of their
background preceding this program, that they have achieved an adequate mastery of the required
knowledge and abilities.

Eligibility requirements for operator licensing training programs serve the dual objectives of 1)
ensuring training program success and 2) providing for a variety of experience and education in the
post-licensure working environment. Regarding the first objective, a SAT-based training program that
is paired with a valid and reliable testing process will, by design, screen candidates that do not have
the competency to adequately perform the job. The implementation and evaluation stages of the
SAT Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) process also assess
candidate performance at the end of the training process and create a programmatic feedback loop
that will adjust the upstream processes (of which candidate selection is a portion) to
achieve acceptable training results. Regarding the second objective, the NextGen Ops Program will
source interns from the college technical programs for senior reactor operator training and augment
their collegiate studies with parallel training on nuclear plant operations topics (including fundamentals
and plant systems). When used in combination with the existing ACAD eligibility pathways, the
NextGen Ops Program will thus populate operating shift crews with a variety of experience and
education.

Taken as a whole, the use of NextEra's NextGen Ops eligibility pathways in combination with the existing
eligibility pathways of ACAD 10-001 will yield an equivalent level of assurance in both individual candidate
competency and aggregate operating crew effectiveness as provided by current license candidate
commitments. Importantly, the guidance documents associated with licensed operator candidate eligibility
under 10 CFR Part 55 (i.e., RG-1.8 prior to Revision 4, NUREG-1021 Revision 12, and ACAD 10-
001 Revision 2) each allow for the use of alternatives. 10 CFR Part 55 does not prescribe the eligibility
requirements for license operator candidates to enter the program beyond the 10 CFR 55.31 (a)(4)
requirement for operator license applications to either provide the details of the applicant's qualifications or,
alternatively, to certify the completion of a Commission-approved training program that is based on a
SAT (e.g., a NANT accredited training program). Thus, an alternative approach to candidate qualification
that is acceptable under a NANT accredited training program (i.e., ACAD 10-001 as endorsed by NUREG-
1021) is adequate for meeting the regulatory requirements of 10 CFR 55.31(a)(4). Thereby, with the
proposed QATR changes implementing the NextGen Ops Program Plan, the quality assurance criteria
of 1O CFR 50, Appendix B, and the Safety Analysis Report quality assurance program description
commitments previously accepted by the NRC will continue to be met.

Enclosure 3, "Senior Reactor Operator Eligibility Pathway Comparisons," provides an overview of the
current ACAD 10-001 SRO eligibility pathways as they compare to the NextGen Ops SRO
eligibility pathway, and categorically shows how equivalent assurance is provided via the added
pathway. Enclosure 4, "Reactor Operator Eligibility Pathway Comparisons," provides a similar

                                  NEXTGEN OPS PROGRAM PLAN
NextGen Ops is NextEra Energy's nuclear-focused development pathway designed to introduce
college students and other NextEra employees to nuclear plant operations. Placed at NextEra nuclear
generating sites, participants work alongside licensed reactor operators and plant staff, learning
fundamentals of NRG-regulated operations, safety culture, and progress toward eventual operator
licensure.

The sections below describe the core elements of the NextGen Ops Program for both SRO and RO
license candidates. NextEra will implement procedures and processes to implement the elements
below as a minimum baseline for the program. Program duration will be determined by the time
required for individuals to satisfactorily complete programmatic content. All plant-related, in-person
activities must occur at the same facility where licensure is intended to occur. While specific details of
individual elements may vary (such as changes brought about by SAT-based analyses), these core
el.ements will not be reduced beyond the levels specified below:

NextGen Ops Senior Reactor Operator Program Core Elements {refer to Figure 1)
    •   Bachelor's degree (or higher) in engineering, engineering technology, or related sciences.
        o   Degree program must be completed prior to issuance of license.
    •   Complete a systematically designed site layout course.
    •   Complete structured observation training (minimum of 240 hours).
        o   This is in addition to the on-the-job training required under the accredited license program.

    •   Perform practical and meaningful work assignments for at least six months.
        o   Must be completed prior to issuance of license.
    •   Complete a structured leadership development training program.

    •   Complete the accredited initial SRO training program.
NextGen Ops Reactor Operator Program Core Elements {refer to Figure 2)

    •   High school diploma or equivalent.
        o   Must be completed prior to program entry.

    •   Complete a systematically designed site layout course.
    •   Complete structured observation training (minimum of 240 hours).
        o   This is in addition to the on-the-job training required under the accredited license program.

    •   Perform practical and meaningful work assignments for at least six months.
        o   Must be completed prior to issuance of license.
    •   Complete site-specific, non-licensed operator (NLO) training for selected tasks.
        o   This is in addition to the on-the-job training required under the accredited license program.

    •   Complete the accredited initial RO training program.
